holidays.name: National Dolphin Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the clever, chatty, perpetually smiling marine mammals of the sea. Watch dolphin videos, learn about ocean conservation, or just make some clicking noises at your pets in tribute.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It has become a yearly favorite among animal lovers and ocean advocates.
holidays.funFact: Dolphins can sleep with half of their brain at a time. One side rests while the other stays alert, so they can keep surfacing to breathe.

holidays.name: National Ex-Spouse Day
holidays.description: A day for making peace with the person who used to share your last name and your streaming password. Send a civil text, let a grudge go, or simply raise a glass to the lessons learned.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It encourages goodwill and closure after a split.
holidays.funFact: The word 'ex' comes from the Latin for 'out of' or 'from', which is why it can be stuck in front of almost any title, from ex-president to ex-roommate.

holidays.name: Look Up at the Sky Day
holidays.description: A call to stop staring at your screen and tilt your head back. Watch the clouds drift, spot a bird, or lie in the grass and wait for the first star to appear.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It fits neatly into the spring season, when skies are at their most dramatic.
holidays.funFact: The daytime sky looks blue because air molecules scatter short-wavelength blue light much more than red light, a effect called Rayleigh scattering.
